title: Console UX: Tiered SLO dashboards for Dedicated (filters + error budget status)
creator: Lauren Bishop
description:
## Context
Dedicated customers (and CS/SE) need a clear, shareable, *account-scoped* view of reliability: tiered SLOs (availability + latency + streaming reliability) and error budget state. This ticket covers Console UX for Dedicated SLO dashboards, aligned to the tiered SLO + error budget program.

Primary pain points driving this:
- Customers asking “Are we meeting our SLO? What counts/excludes?” (see SUP-28412)
- Escalations where a regional spike happens and CS/SE can’t quickly confirm impact/scope (SUP-28455)
- Confusion around streaming disconnect accounting (SUP-28501)

## Goals
- Provide a Dedicated-focused SLO landing page with clear tier badge + reporting window.
- Make it easy to slice by Region / Endpoint class / Model (with guardrails to avoid cardinality traps).
- Surface error budget state with consistent, accessible status badges, and link to “what this means” definitions.
- Enable fast triage: show top contributors (models/routes/regions) and link to traces/logs where permitted.
- Support internal sharing (CS/SE/SRE) with stable URLs and a “copy link” affordance.

## Non-goals
- Designing SLO calculations or exclusions (owned by SRE standards docs / ENG tickets).
- Building customer-facing SLA language (covered in the SLO↔SLA mapping doc).
- A full incident communications UX (status page lives elsewhere; we only link out).

## Proposed IA / Navigation
- Console left nav: **Reliability → SLOs**
  - If user has Dedicated accounts: default to **Dedicated SLOs**.
  - If user only has Hosted usage: route to Hosted reliability view (future/handled elsewhere).

## Page layout (Dedicated SLOs)
### 1) Header strip (always visible)
- Account selector (Dedicated account)
- Tier badge: “Dedicated” (non-editable)
- Reporting window selector: default **28d**; quick picks: 1h, 6h, 24h, 7d, 28d
- Last updated timestamp + data freshness indicator
- “Definitions” link (opens side panel) with:
  - What counts as success/error
  - Exclusions: invalid requests, rate-limited, client aborts (explicitly called out)
  - Streaming reliability definition + how disconnects are classified

### 2) Filters row
Filters are ordered by likelihood of use and impact on query cost:
- **Region** (multi-select, default: All regions enabled for the account)
- **Endpoint class** (segmented): Chat/Completions | Embeddings | Rerank | Streaming (if applicable)
- **Model** (typeahead; default “All models”; results capped; show “Top models by traffic” first)
- Optional (collapsed under “More”): Route (read-only surfaced only if backend provides safe aggregation)

Guardrails:
- If user selects >5 models, show non-blocking warning: “Large model filter may reduce performance; results may be sampled.”
- If query results are sampled/limited, show inline note with link “Why?”

### 3) Error budget status module (prominent)
A single, consistent status badge with a short explanation and key numbers.

**Badge states (copy + semantics):**
- **Healthy**: budget remaining above threshold; no active burn alerts
- **At risk**: elevated burn rate; budget likely to exhaust if trend continues
- **Burning**: burn-rate alert firing (multi-window); requires mitigation
- **Exhausted**: budget spent for window; release freeze may be active

Module contents:
- Status badge + one-line explanation
- Budget remaining (% and minutes) for the selected window
- Current burn rate (if burning/at risk), showing the window pair (e.g., 1h/6h)
- Links:
  - “View active alerts” (internal only)
  - “Mitigation runbook” (internal; opens in new tab)
  - “Share view” (copy URL)

Accessibility:
- Badge must not rely on color alone; include icon + text.
- Colors align with existing Console severity tokens (confirm with design system).

### 4) SLO scorecards (per SLI)
Show 3–4 tiles depending on endpoint class:
- **Availability / Success rate** (non-5xx definition; show exclusions via tooltip)
- **Latency**: p50 / p95 / p99 (Dedicated target shown; actual vs target)
- **Streaming reliability** (only for streaming): disconnect rate + server-side error events
- Optional: “Overload / shed rate” (internal-only, if we decide it’s helpful and safe)

Each tile includes:
- Current value for selected window
- Target value (SLO)
- Trend sparkline
- “View details” anchor to the time series section

### 5) Time series + annotations
A unified chart area with tabs:
- Availability
- Latency
- Streaming reliability (if applicable)

Features:
- Hover tooltips include numerator/denominator (where safe), and a link “See breakdown”.
- Annotations row: deploys + incidents + major routing policy changes (pull from existing annotations feed).

### 6) Breakdown / top contributors
Goal: “What changed?” without exploding cardinality.

Default breakdown tables (Top 5 + ‘View more’):
- By region
- By model (limited list)
- By route (only if routes are safely grouped; else omit)
- By error class (5xx family, timeouts, upstream disconnects)

Each row:
- Contribution to budget spend (or error count)
- Delta vs previous period
- Quick link: “Open traces” (if user has access)

## Empty/error states
- No data for selection: “No SLO data for this filter set (yet). Try expanding window or clearing Model filter.”
- Partial instrumentation: show “Data incomplete” banner with affected regions/endpoints listed.
- Permissions: CS/SE without account access should see an access request CTA (ties into INT-9331 process; copy only).

## Shareable URLs
- URL should encode: account, window, region(s), endpoint class, model(s).
- Provide “Copy link” button. For internal sharing, include a “You may not have access” note.

## Deliverables
- Figma: Dedicated SLOs landing page + components (badge states, filters, scorecards)
- Interaction spec: filter behavior, sampling warnings, empty states
- Copy deck: exact strings for badge explanations + definitions panel
- Engineering handoff notes (data requirements and query constraints)

## Open questions
1) Do we show “budget remaining” as both % and minutes, or only %?
2) Should latency targets be displayed as a single number (p95) by default with p50/p99 in details, or show all three on the tile?
3) What is the minimal set of breakdowns we can reliably provide without stressing the metrics system?

## References / links
- Confluence: tiered SLO dashboard/alerts spec (for visual parity)
- Confluence: SLI specification (definitions for exclusions + streaming)
- Linear deps: ENG-4946 (dedicated customer SLO dashboards), ENG-4934 (budget computation job)

## Acceptance criteria
- Dedicated SLO dashboard supports Region / Endpoint class / Model filters with stable URLs.
- Error budget status badge states are implemented with final copy and accessibility requirements.
- Scorecards + charts reflect the selected filter context and clearly show target vs actual.
- Empty/error states are defined and approved by SRE + PM Dedicated.
- Handoff includes explicit backend requirements (what aggregations are needed; what must be capped).
comments: 2026-01-24 (Lauren Bishop): Customer asks keep coming in for “proof” we’re tracking SLOs per Dedicated account. Need something CS can screenshot/share that’s consistent with the new policy. Please prioritize error budget status clarity (Healthy/At risk/Burning/Exhausted) and keep the math behind a definitions panel.

2026-01-28 (Sergio Costa): +1 on guardrails. Please don’t expose raw route IDs by default; we’ve had cardinality issues. Top-N is OK if we group routes into stable buckets (e.g., /v1/chat, /v1/embeddings) rather than per-customer custom routes.

2026-02-02 (Rachel Kim): For escalations, Region + Model are the first two questions every time. Also need a clear answer on streaming disconnects vs client aborts—support tickets keep getting stuck here.

2026-02-06 (Aisha Bello): Badge states should align with burn-rate alerting: “Burning” means an alert is active (multi-window). “Exhausted” should imply freeze policy may apply. Please include a link to runbook and to the current alert(s).

2026-02-11 (Felix Schneider): From backend side we can provide: account_id, tier, region, endpoint_class, model_family (not full model name for all views), plus top-5 models by traffic. Full model list might be too heavy unless we gate it behind a separate query.

2026-02-14 (Chloe Martin): Drafts in Figma ready for review. Key call: header has account selector + window + ‘Definitions’ panel; filters row includes Region + Endpoint class + Model (typeahead, capped). Scorecards show p95 by default with p50/p99 in tooltip/details to keep scannable.

2026-02-18 (Nikhil Sharma): Please ensure Hosted vs Dedicated visual treatment is distinct; we don’t want Hosted customers inferring Dedicated commitments. Even if this page is Dedicated-only, tier should be explicit and non-editable.
updates: 2026-02-07: Aligned with SRE on badge semantics and that ‘Burning’ maps to active burn-rate alert firing. Added explicit link targets (alerts/runbook) and accessibility requirements.
2026-02-14: Completed first pass layout + components (filters, badge, scorecards, chart annotations, breakdown tables). Added guardrails for model filter to avoid expensive queries.

2026-02-18: Incorporated PM + CS feedback: Region/Model prioritized; streaming reliability definitions moved into a side panel with explicit examples (disconnect vs client abort). Ready for eng handoff review.
handoff_notes: Eng needs to confirm which dimensions are safe to expose as filters vs breakdown-only. Proposed constraints: model filter defaults to ‘All models’ and only supports selecting from top models by traffic unless explicitly expanded. Breakdowns limited to Top 5 with a stable grouping key (e.g., model_family). Charts should support annotations feed (deploys/incidents/routing policy changes). Provide data freshness + ‘incomplete data’ signals from telemetry pipeline.
